intended_object: For a continuous homomorphism φ : H → G, a continuous G-representation V and a continuous H-equivariant map f : Res_φ V → W, this is the induced continuous H-equivariant map between the co-induced modules, Res_φ C(G, V) → C(H, W), given by F ↦ f ∘ F ∘ φ. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is the composite `(coind₁Map f).comp (coind₁Res φ π)`. Here `coind₁Res` is precomposition with φ, i.e. `ContinuousMap.compCLM`, and it intertwines the actions. `coind₁Map f` is postcomposition with f. So the map sends F to f ∘ F ∘ φ, which is exactly what the docstring says; the lemma `coind₁ResMap_apply` holds by `rfl`.

`coind₁` puts on C(G, V) the action (g·F)(x) = π(g)(F(g⁻¹x)). The restriction of this action along φ agrees with the H-action on C(H, W), so f ∘ F ∘ φ is H-equivariant. This is the standard map between co-induced modules attached to a compatible pair (φ, f), as used for restriction and inflation in continuous cohomology.

The setting is the right one: topological groups G and H, any ring R, and topological modules. The construction needs these assumptions, since it uses inverses in the coinduced action and continuous maps. I found no more general version of this map in Mathlib.
